newsitem.title: USA: February manufacturing faster, prices gain - NAPM.
newsitem.headline: February manufacturing faster, prices gain - NAPM.

text.p: The U.S. manufacturing sector grew more quickly in February, with gains in production and other areas as well as a rise in prices, the National Association of Purchasing Management said on Monday.

The group of executives who buy materials for the nation's factories said its index of maufacturing activity rose to 53.1 in February from 52.0 in January. A reading above 50 percent indicates growth, while one below 50 percent signals contraction.

"The manufacturing sector grew more rapidly in February than in January with production and new orders indicating an increase in growth," said Norbert Ore, chair of the NAPM's Business Survey Committee.
"However, prices paid were higher, with 13 industries reporting that they are paying higher prices. Employment continued to decline at a faster rate."
The surprisingly strong report depressed the bond market, which feared it would prompt the Federal Reserve to raise interest rates to moderate economic growth.
The 30-year Treasury bond fell 12/32, raising the yield to 6.83 percent from 6.80 percent at Friday's close.
NAPM's production index edged up 1.4 percentage points to 59.5 percent as output increased. Its new orders index grew 4.2 percentage points to 57.7 percent.
The backlog of orders index reflected less volume of unfilled orders for the seventh time in eight months during February, with the index moving up to 48.5 percent.
NAPM's supplier deliveries index in February rose to 51.3 percent from 48.5 percent, as deliveries slowed.
NAPM's employment index marked the 24th consecutive month in which manufacturing employment fell, with a drop to 45.4 percent in February from 48.7 percent in January.
NAPM's price index in February climbed to 55.1 percent, signalling higher prices for the third month in a row.
NAPM's inventories index slowed to 41.2 percent from 44.4 percent in January.

Asked about customers' inventories of products purchased from manufacturers, 13 percent of respondents felt they were too high, up from 11 percent in January. However, 24 percent, up from 18 percent in January, felt they were too low, and 63 percent, down from 71 percent in January, thought they were about right.

NAPM said its new export orders index slid to 52.1 percent from 54.6 percent, and has stayed above 50 above for the past 12 months. Imports of materials by manufacturers declined as NAPM's imports index fell to 50.9 percent from 51.8 percent in January, but remained above 50 percent.

Of the 20 manufacturing industries, 11 reported an improvement in February. These were petroleum; jewelry, toys, sporting goods and musical instruments; textiles; wood and wood products; chemicals; apparel; industrial and commercial equipment and computers; printing and publishing; leather; plastics; and transportation and equipment.
